question: What is the central organizational idea behind Data Mesh?
options: Centralizing all data ownership in a single platform team
Decentralizing data ownership to domain teams who own their data as products
Eliminating governance entirely
Storing all data in one monolithic data lake owned by IT
explanation: Data Mesh shifts ownership from a central team to the business domains that produce the data, treating data as a product owned end-to-end by domain teams. It is a sociotechnical/organizational shift, not a single technology.

question: The 'data as a product' principle in Data Mesh requires that domain data products be:
options: Kept private within each team and never shared
Discoverable, addressable, trustworthy, and well-documented for consumers to use self-serve
Stored only as raw unprocessed logs
Manually copied on request by a central team
explanation: Treating data as a product means each domain publishes datasets with product qualities: discoverable, addressable, self-describing, trustworthy (SLAs/quality), and secure, so other teams can consume them without bottlenecks.

question: 'Federated computational governance' in Data Mesh means:
options: One central board manually approves every dataset
Governance is abandoned in favor of full autonomy
Global standards and policies are defined collectively but enforced automatically and locally by each domain and the platform
Each domain invents its own incompatible rules with no coordination
explanation: Federated computational governance balances domain autonomy with global interoperability: cross-domain standards (security, quality, interoperability) are agreed federally and encoded into the platform so they're enforced automatically, not by a central gatekeeper.

question: The self-serve data platform pillar exists in Data Mesh to:
options: Give domain teams tooling/infrastructure to build and serve data products without deep platform expertise, avoiding central bottlenecks
Force all domains to write their own low-level infrastructure
Replace domain ownership with a central data team
Store data exclusively on individual laptops
explanation: A self-serve platform provides domain-agnostic infrastructure and tooling (storage, pipelines, cataloging, access) so autonomous domains can produce data products efficiently, lowering the skill barrier and removing central dependencies.

question: For which organization is Data Mesh generally LEAST appropriate?
options: A large enterprise with many distinct domains and a central data team that is a chronic bottleneck
A company with numerous autonomous product teams each owning rich data
An organization struggling to scale analytics across many business units
A small startup with one small team and a modest, centralized dataset
explanation: Data Mesh's benefits come from decentralizing across many domains; its overhead (federated governance, platform, per-domain ownership) is not justified for a small team with a single modest dataset, where a centralized approach is simpler and cheaper.
